question: Which native instruction-budget projection preserves a rule, and can native lazy skill loading restore rule-dependent task quality after instruction omission?
thinking: disabled through public native configuration for both products

limit_semantics.DSH: UTF-8 bytes per rendered instruction chain, framing included
limit_semantics.OpenClaw: UTF-16 characters per bootstrap file; total bootstrap cap separately fixed at 65536

fixture_alphabet: ASCII, so source bytes and UTF-16 character counts agree; renderer framing and selection still differ
fixture: One random block-specific codec rule in the middle of a long AGENTS.md and in a matching skill; held-out integer inputs shared across every arm of that block. Same content except explicit Required keyword diagnostic. Rule absent from initial user prompt and skill description. Redundancy is deliberately constructed to identify recovery through a second native context route.

skill_control.DSH: skill-filesystem includeDefaultRoots=false; customSkillDirs selects the owned fixture root or an empty list; watch=false
skill_control.OpenClaw: skills.allowBundled=[probe-codec] (nonempty sentinel allowlist excludes unrelated bundled skills); skills.entries.probe-codec.enabled selects the owned project skill

task: Common user prompt supplies checksum=(sum(values)*factor+offset)%997 and string format prefix:checksum. Random prefix/factor/offset must come only from supplied project instructions or advertised native skill. Load the skill if advertised. Do not read AGENTS.md/search/shell/invent. JSON encoded string or null if unknown.

acceptance.delivery: Normal exit and a single JSON object with only encoded key, string or null; optional surrounding whitespace or Markdown JSON fence allowed by this preregistration
acceptance.quality: encoded exactly equals independently computed prefix plus (sum(values)*factor+offset) modulo 997; null is a delivered but incomplete result
acceptance.constraint: No tool except exact fixture native skill loader (DSH skill or OpenClaw skills_read with name=probe-codec) or OpenClaw read of advertised fixture SKILL.md; only when fixture skill enabled. Unknown names, other paths, direct AGENTS read, shell and search violate task constraints.
acceptance.calibration_gate: Actual ample neutral rule visible in both products, tight neutral omitted in both, required-keyword diagnostic retained by OpenClaw policy digest but omitted by DSH; advertised skill invoked and its actual result contains rule. Every arm has complete cgroup collection and expected fixture-derived delivery/quality.
acceptance.real_run: Record all quality/constraint outcomes, including failures. Do not change predicate after observing real outputs. Native resource or adapter errors remain separate from model task failure.

analysis: Publish all independent block points. Within-product paired contrasts: ample/tight with skill disabled; skill enabled/disabled at each budget; difference-in-differences for constructed redundancy; Required keyword diagnostic at tight/no-skill. Two blocks support mechanism observations only, not a broad quality/performance ranking or population-level significance claim.
measurement: Task submission to independently timestamped delivery check; separate process exit; real per-request input/output/cache usage including title calls; cgroup CPU, PSS/RSS, kernel memory peak, sampled disk and raw I/O; controller+relay process CPU separately. Record source payload sizes as bytes, not tokens. Dedicated memory-reader command CPU is a disjoint observer child cost; sampling thread is an overlapping parent-process subset, never added twice.
ordering: Randomized arm order per paired block, seed retained. Products share pinned installation; cache state is not reset globally.
exclusions: This is instruction/bootstrap budgeting and skill availability/loading. It does not test cumulative task-tree hard quotas, dynamic skill policy optimization, full context-window compaction, native self-improvement, or rollback.
scheduling: Admit complete comparison block; no generic real-task timeout. Synthetic protocol calibration has a declared 120-second settlement safeguard. Native configuration and transport bounds retained.
instrumentation_revision: r3: common public algorithm makes ample/no-skill a fully specified positive control; exact native skill loader binding includes OpenClaw skills_read and path reads. Synthetic provider prefers exposed native name loader. New study with new random held-out blocks; CTX-01 raw judgments unchanged.

prior_exploration.disposition: No causal quality credit: missing common algorithm and incomplete native skill loader scoring; all original data retained.
